newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's BLOM bank doubles capital to $150 mln.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's BLOM bank doubles capital to $150 mln.

text.p: Lebanon's Banque du Liban et d'Outre Mer (BLOM) said on Wednesday it had doubled its capital to $150 million.
"Shareholders' equity increased from $77 million to over $150 million," the bank said in a statement.
The increase took place at the end of 1996, it said.

It lifted BLOM to second from fourth place among Lebanon's 82 banks in terms of capital, behind Banque de la Mediterranee which more than doubled its capital at the end of 1996 to $212 million from $102 million.
The third-placed bank in terms of capital is Banque Audi, with $63 million.
BLOM was Lebanon's biggest bank in terms of customer deposits in 1995, according to Bilanbanques 1996, a compilation of data on the Lebanese banking sector.
It has 31 branches in Lebanon and one in Cyprus and has 840 employees, according to the Almanac of the Lebanese Banks Association.
